ComoUsar.title: How to Use the Text Counter
ComoUsar.intro: Using Use Count Me is simple and instant. No registration or extension installation is required:

steps.step1Text: Enter the content directly into the main text box.
steps.step2Title: Check the metrics in real time:
steps.step2Text: Character counts (with and without spaces), words, and sentences are updated automatically as you type.

actions.copyText: Sends the content directly to your device's clipboard.
actions.clearText: Empties the text area so you can start a new count.
actions.formatText: Quickly switch the text to uppercase (UPPERCASE) or lowercase (lowercase).

ComoUsar.conclusion: Because the tool focuses on accurate metrics and efficiency, we have kept the interface clean and straightforward, making it ideal for quickly reviewing academic papers, social media posts, and articles.

Etimologia.title: Etymology: The Origins of the Words We Count
Etimologia.intro: Have you ever wondered where the terms we use every day when writing a document come from? The history behind the vocabulary of writing is fascinating and dates back to classical antiquity.
Etimologia.palavraText: comes from the Vulgar Latin paraula, which in turn derives from the Classical Latin parabola (meaning "comparison," "discourse," or "allegory"). The latter word has roots in the Ancient Greek parabolē (parabolē), meaning "to place beside" or "to compare." Over the centuries, the term evolved from the concept of comparison to designate the basic unit of speech and writing.
Etimologia.textoText: comes from the Latin textus, which literally means "fabric," "weave," or "woven material." The term derives from the Latin verb texere ("to weave"). The analogy is both poetic and precise: just as individual threads are woven together to form cloth, words and sentences are woven together by the author to create a coherent work.
Etimologia.caractereText: (or character) comes from the Ancient Greek kharaktēr, a term used for the tool used to engrave, mark, or stamp coins and symbols. Later, it came to mean the engraved sign itself or the distinctive mark of something—giving rise both to the typographical characters we count and to the concept of human "character."

FAQ.title: Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)
FAQ.q1Title: Is the text I type saved on any server?
FAQ.q1Text: All processing is performed exclusively in your own browser (client-side). The text you type is not sent to, read by, or stored on any external server. We only use local sessionStorage to prevent you from losing your progress if you accidentally reload the page, but everything is deleted when you close the tab.
FAQ.q2Text: The tool is 100% free with no usage limits. You do not need to create an account, log in, or provide personal information to use all its features.
FAQ.q3Title: How are words and sentences counted?
FAQ.q3Text: The word count identifies the spaces and punctuation marks that separate terms. The sentence count identifies the periods, question marks, and exclamation marks that delimit each sentence in your text.
FAQ.q4Title: Can I use the tool on my phone?
FAQ.q4Text: The website layout is fully responsive and adapted to work well on computers, tablets, and smartphones.

PqUsar.title: Why Use a Word and Character Counter?
PqUsar.intro: In many everyday situations, we need to produce content that meets strict length limits. Counting words or characters manually is inefficient and prone to errors. Use Count Me automates this process with absolute accuracy.

applications.socialText: Each platform has its own text limits, such as X/Twitter, Instagram, LinkedIn, and Meta Ads. Using the counter prevents your captions or ads from being cut off.
applications.academicText: Essays, abstracts, and articles often require a minimum or maximum number of words to comply with academic standards.
applications.seoText: Writers and marketing professionals need to keep meta descriptions, article titles, and blog posts within the ideal length for search engines.
applications.formsText: Applications for jobs, scholarships, or project submissions often impose strict limits on text fields.

PqUsar.privacy: In addition to providing instant metrics, the tool runs entirely locally in your browser, ensuring privacy for confidential drafts or personal documents.

VisaoAutor.title: The Author's Perspective and Motivation
VisaoAutor.intro: Use Count Me was created from the desire to combine practical utility with continuous improvement in modern web development.

items.logicText: Implementation of real-time string manipulation and predictable state management with React.
items.archText: Exploration of the App Router, modular component organization, and optimization for SEO and performance.
items.uxText: Building a clean and responsive design with CSS, focused on a straightforward user experience.
items.seoText: Practical application of search engine optimization strategies using the Next.js Metadata API, structured data architecture, and navigation files such as sitemap.xml and robots.txt for maximum organic visibility.
items.lifecycleText: From the conception of the code to deployment in production, with preparation for integrating analytics and advertisements.

VisaoAutor.conclusion: Besides serving as a functional everyday tool, this project is an important milestone in building my portfolio as a developer.
